verification.notes: hec.gov.pk could not be reached from this environment on any attempt (curl, headless browser and reader proxies all timed out, and the Google translate proxy returned a 408 from the origin), so official HEC content was obtained from the Wayback Machine snapshot of HEC's own CAFC page (17 June 2026), from the search-engine index of HEC's own AMIC sub-pages, and from the HEC-authored 'Study in Pakistan on a FULLY FUNDED SCHOLARSHIP' advertisement hosted on the Government of Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs site (dated 20 July 2026), corroborated by the Embassy of Pakistan, Ashgabat page on mofa.gov.pk and by UET Lahore's admissions portal. Benefit structure, eligibility thresholds and the 10 August 2026 deadline were consistent across all of these; no stipend amount is published anywhere.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a Government of Pakistan route into a BS degree at a Pakistani public university with tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one airfare and a one-off settlement payment all covered - money you would otherwise have to raise for the full four years yourself. The gate is academic, not financial: HEC's 2026 advertisement fixed entry at A-Levels or equivalent with at least 60% marks (65% for Engineering), so your percentage decides whether you enter the pool at all before any interview happens. Be aware that the only dated round HEC published closed on 10 August 2026 and no postgraduate or doctoral round appeared on any page that could be read, so undergraduate applicants should treat this as a watch-and-wait target while MS and PhD candidates should look elsewhere. Because HEC publishes no stipend figure, you must be able to absorb personal spending, visa costs and anything beyond tuition and accommodation even if you win.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Central Asian (and listed friendly-country) school leavers with strong A-Level results who want a fully funded English-medium BS in Pakistan and can tolerate HEC's slow, multi-year rollout.
application_readiness_checklist: Calculate your A-Level/equivalent aggregate now and confirm it clears 60% (or 65% for Engineering) - HEC fixes this threshold in the advert itself, so a 59% aggregate is fatal regardless of anything else.
Confirm your country is on HEC's current eligible-country list on the AMIC Introduction page before investing any effort - the list has been edited between programme stages.
Start the IBCC equivalence route early: HEC requires an IBCC Equivalence Certificate after award, and converting foreign qualifications is the most common cause of delay at enrolment and visa stage.
Watch HEC's CAFC and AMIC pages plus HEC's news/press-release page for the next advert - HEC has been opening BS rounds in July with an August cut-off.
Lock in the email address and phone number you will register in HEC's portal, since shortlisting, test/interview invitations and award letters all run through that single channel.
Put round-specific questions to HEC directly at studyinpak@hec.gov.pk or +92 51 90408036 (Project Director, Mr. Jehanzeb Khan) rather than to social-media reposts.
common_rejection_risks: Missing the published last date: HEC's advert sets a hard calendar cut-off (10 August 2026 for the last round) and late applications are not entertained.
Falling below the 60%/65% aggregate in your A-Level or equivalent result - HEC publishes the threshold in the advert, leaving no discretion route.
Applying for a discipline outside the advertised field groups; the 2026 round named exactly seven groups and anything outside them had no funded seat.
Assuming the award covers everything: tuition, accommodation, stipend, one airfare and settlement support are covered, but visa fees, insurance, attestation costs and family travel are not.
Overlooking an HEC test or interview invitation, which is communicated only through the portal and the registered email.
Trusting aggregator pages that recycle the advert with invented stipend amounts or stale deadlines - HEC publishes no stipend amount at all.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: HEC's published package covers tuition, accommodation, a monthly stipend, one airfare and a one-off settlement payment. Applicants still fund their own visa and residence-permit fees, passport, medical insurance where required, IBCC equivalence and document attestation charges, any travel to and from Pakistan beyond the single provided airfare, and all personal spending and family costs. Because no stipend rate is published, the stipend cannot be checked against local living costs before you commit.
document_audit: Your A-Level or equivalent certificate must sit inside the IBCC equivalence system; HEC requires the certificate only after award, but you need the conversion paperwork ready before you travel because it gates enrolment.

HEC publishes no document checklist on the AMIC pages, so assume the portal will ask for identity evidence, full academic transcripts and equivalence confirmation, and keep certified English translations of every certificate.
Passport validity matters: this is an international-student scheme requiring entry to Pakistan on a student visa, and a passport near expiry stalls both the award and the visa.
Keep the name spelling, email and phone number identical across your portal profile and every uploaded document - mismatches are a routine reason HEC correspondence never reaches applicants.
alerts: The last date HEC published for the 2026 BS round was 10 August 2026 and that date has passed - do not build a plan around a 2026/2027 intake until HEC publishes a new advertisement.
HEC publishes no stipend amount anywhere, so any figure quoting 'PKR ... per month' for this scheme is not from HEC.

Several different programmes share the Iqbal name - the Afghan-student Allama Iqbal Scholarship, the Pakistan-Bangladesh Knowledge Corridor awards and HEC's domestic schemes have different rules, amounts and deadlines; read the CAFC/AMIC pages, not a generic 'Allama Iqbal Scholarship' listing.

The CAFC programme bundles four components (student scholarships, semester exchange, higher education expos, civil-servant leadership training), so search results mixing them under one heading will mislead you.
